analysis.investment_thesis: Clear Secured is a low-margin, commoditised facility management business that has tripled its debt in two years (₹44→₹128 Cr) to fund aggressive expansion, while generating negative free cash flow every single year. Falling net profit in FY25 (₹10 Cr vs ₹12 Cr prior year) despite 37% revenue growth signals the expansion is destroying, not creating, value.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 73% — aligned and committed
ROCE of 20.4% is respectable for a services business
Revenue has nearly doubled in two years (₹309→₹476 Cr), showing clear demand
key_risks: Debt-to-Equity of ~0.94x (₹128/₹136 Cr) — far exceeds my hard limit of 0.3; debt tripled in 2 years
Free cash flow negative all three years (–₹3, –₹7, –₹26 Cr); business consumes cash, not generates it
Net profit fell to ₹10 Cr in FY25 despite 37% revenue growth — finance costs jumped 150% (₹4→₹10 Cr), eroding earnings quality
red_flags: D/E ~0.94x — automatic disqualifier under my framework
OCF positive in only 1 of 3 years; FCF deeply negative and worsening
Earnings declined while revenues surged — a classic sign of over-leveraged expansion
CWIP jumped from ₹1→₹22 Cr — heavy unproductive capital locked up
Operating margin only ~6.5% (₹31/₹476 Cr) — below my minimum threshold of 8%
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Clear Secured fails my most fundamental test: a business must generate cash, not consume it. Three consecutive years of negative free cash flow (–₹3, –₹7, –₹26 Cr) while borrowings tripled from ₹44 Cr to ₹128 Cr in two years is not growth — it is a debt-funded illusion of scale. The facility management sector is commoditised, labour-intensive, and offers no pricing power or brand moat. An operating margin of 6.5% leaves no buffer for error, and finance costs eating nearly the entire operating profit (₹10 Cr finance cost vs ₹31 Cr operating income) is deeply troubling.

What concerns me most is the FY25 net profit actually declining to ₹10 Cr from ₹12 Cr despite a ₹128 Cr revenue jump — that is precisely the pattern I avoid. When revenue grows 37% and profit shrinks, the marginal business being added is value-destructive. The ₹22 Cr in CWIP and continued negative cash flows suggest this pattern will persist. At ₹243 Cr market cap, this is a small, leveraged, cash-burning services company in a sector I have never favoured. I will not invest here.
